post.description:
Create a new agent organization with an inbox and API key. This endpoint is for signing up for the first time. If you've already signed up, you're all set — just use your existing API key.

A 6-digit OTP is sent to the human's email for verification.

The new organization starts with 1 inbox, no custom domains, and 10 emails per day, which can be sent only to `human_email` until the organization is verified.

`human_email` is optional. Without it, the inbox can receive email but cannot send to anyone until a human is attached with the attach human endpoint or, for a US-region inbox, claims it in the AgentMail Console with the API key (see [How do I claim my agent's inbox?](https://docs.agentmail.to/knowledge-base/claiming-agent-inbox)). There is also no way to recover the API key, so store it durably. Calling sign-up again without `human_email` creates a new organization, which needs a different `username`: the original username stays with the lost organization's inbox.

This endpoint is idempotent. Calling it again with the same `human_email` will rotate the API key and resend the OTP if expired.

The returned API key has limited permissions until the organization is verified via the verify endpoint.

**CLI:**
```bash
agentmail agent sign-up --human-email user@example.com --username my-agent
```

Attach a human to an unverified agent organization. A 6-digit OTP is sent to the human's email, which you then submit to the verify endpoint.

Use it after signing up without a `human_email`. Once the human is attached, the organization can send email to that human only, and verification lifts the remaining restrictions. For up to 5 minutes after attaching, sends to the human can still be rejected with a `429` daily send limit error while the API key's cached limits catch up. Wait and retry.

Calling it again with the same `human_email` does not rotate the API key. It resends the OTP if it was never delivered, or issues a new one if it expired. While the current OTP is still valid, calling it again keeps that OTP and its attempt count. If all 10 attempts are used up, wait until the OTP expires, 24 hours after it was issued, then call it again for a new one.

Calling it with a different `human_email` replaces the attached human and sends the new human an OTP. An organization can replace its human at most 2 times.

Only available until the organization is verified.

**CLI:**
```bash
agentmail agent attach-human --human-email user@example.com
```

Verify an agent organization using the 6-digit OTP sent to the human's email during sign-up.

On success, the organization is upgraded from `agent_unverified` to `agent_verified`, the send allowlist is removed, and the Free plan's entitlements are applied: 3 inboxes and 100 emails per day, at first to at most 3 distinct recipients in the first hour, 5 in the first day, and 10 in the first week.

The OTP expires after 24 hours and allows a maximum of 10 attempts. If the OTP expired, call the attach human endpoint with the same `human_email` to get a new one without rotating the API key. Once all 10 attempts are used, even the correct OTP is rejected, and attach human keeps returning the same OTP until it expires, so wait for it to expire before asking for a new one. An organization that signed up without a `human_email` has no OTP until a human is attached. If you run into any difficulties receiving the OTP code, you can also create an account on [console.agentmail.to](https://console.agentmail.to) using the human email address you provided to verify your account.

**CLI:**
```bash
agentmail agent verify --otp-code 123456
```

Starts an upload: creates a pending file at `path` and returns an `upload` to `PUT` its bytes to. The bytes go
straight to storage, not through the API. Then call Complete File to make the file `ready`.

Retry-safe: sending the identical request again (same `path`, `size`, `sha256`, `content_type` and
`expires_at`) returns the existing file with `200` instead of `201`: a pending one with a fresh `upload`, or
a `ready` one without. If its bytes were uploaded but the upload was never completed, it is completed then. A
different request at a path whose file is still pending and has no bytes replaces that file; at any other
taken path it returns `409`.

The file counts against the organization's Drive quota from creation, pending or not: 1 GiB and 10,000 files
by default. A file that doesn't fit returns `403` with code `limit_exceeded`. Deleting a file frees its
space within seconds. Expired files count until a create needs their space: a create that doesn't fit first
gives back what expired files hold, a batch at a time, so retry a refusal while many expired files remain.

Requires the `file_create` permission, which an unverified organization's keys don't have at any scope until
it completes agent verification. A key without `file_read` can still create files, but gets the plain `409` at
any taken path, even for an identical request at a file it didn't create.

Agent Drive is in AgentMail Labs, available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`) but not yet in EU
production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

403.description:
`code` says why: `forbidden` when the organization hasn't joined AgentMail Labs; `missing_permission` when the
credential lacks the file permission the endpoint needs, including `file_create` in an organization that hasn't
completed agent verification, and every file permission for an organization- or pod-scoped key under a
content-access policy; `account_suspended`, `pod_suspended` or `inbox_suspended` when the organization, pod or
inbox is suspended; and, for Create File only, `limit_exceeded` when the file doesn't fit the organization's
Drive quota.

expires_at.description:
When the file expires, in the future. Rounded up to a whole second and returned in UTC. On a retry, send
the `expires_at` the first response returned.

get.description:
Lists the inbox's files in path order, pending ones included, optionally only those whose path starts with
`path_prefix`. A prefix matches characters, not whole segments: `reports/q` matches `reports/q3.pdf`. Items
carry no download URL; get a file for one.

The list is read in the region that serves the request, so a file created or deleted a moment ago may not
show yet. Expired files never show.

Requires the `file_read` permission.

parameters.description: Only files whose path starts with this. Held to the path rules, except it may stop partway.

parameters.name: ascending

post.description:
Makes a pending file `ready` once its bytes are uploaded, and returns it, with its `download_url` if the key
has `file_read`. Calling it on a file that is already `ready` returns the file.

Returns `409` if the bytes haven't been uploaded yet, or if what was uploaded doesn't match the file's `size`
and `sha256`. Returns `404` for a file that has expired or was deleted, including a pending file not
completed within a day of its creation.

Requires the `file_create` permission. Only a key with `file_read`, or the key that created the file, can
complete it; any other key gets `404`.

Counts of email events (sent, delivered, bounced, etc.) over time for
the inbox. Defaults to the last 24 hours; `start` must be within the
last 90 days, and a future `end` is clamped to now. Omit `period` for
individual event counts, or set it to sum counts into buckets of that
many seconds.

**CLI:**
```bash
agentmail inboxes metrics query-events --inbox-id <inbox_id>
```

Cumulative usage series for the inbox. Each point is the running total
of the usage type at that timestamp, not the change within the bucket.
Inbox-scoped queries carry `storage_bytes`, `message_count`, and
`thread_count`; requested types that don't apply to the scope are
ignored. Defaults to the last 24 hours; `start` must be within the
last 90 days, and a future `end` is clamped to now. The range divided
by `period` must not exceed 1000 buckets.

Rolling bounce and complaint rates for the inbox. At each `period`
grid point, the bounced (or complained) messages over the preceding
`window` divided by the messages sent over the same window, with the
send count alongside. Account moderation evaluates the organization-wide
rate, so use the organization endpoint to see the number it acts on;
the inbox view shows which inboxes contribute. Defaults to the rolling
24-hour rate sampled hourly over the last day; `start` must be within
the last 90 days, `window` must be a whole multiple of `period`, and
the range plus window divided by `period` must not exceed 1000
buckets.

**CLI:**
```bash
agentmail inboxes metrics query-rates --inbox-id <inbox_id>
```

created. Its `etag` (also the `ETag` response header) is the value to send in `If-Match` to
make an update conditional.

Requires the `calendar_read` permission. Calendar is in AgentMail Labs, available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`)
but not yet in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined
Labs receive a `403`.

key lacks the required calendar permission.

patch.description:
Updates the calendar's default time zone. Existing events keep their own `timezone`; only
events created later without a `timezone` use the new default.

Requires the `calendar_update` permission. To make the update conditional, send the
calendar's current `etag` in `If-Match`: a stale value returns `412`. Without `If-Match` the
update applies to the calendar as it is.

Calendar is in AgentMail Labs, available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`) but not yet
in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

parameters.description: The calendar's current `etag`, for example `"rv-0"`. Optional; makes the update conditional; `*` matches any current version.

get.description:
Lists the events stored on the calendar: one item per one-off or recurring event, plus one
item for each edited date of a recurring event (as that dated event, with
`is_exception: true`). Ordered by most recently updated, and cancelled events are included.
Use it to sync or manage what you created. To see what is on the calendar in a time window,
use Get Agenda.

The list is always read in the region that serves the request, so it can trail a change made
moments earlier by a few seconds. Requires the `calendar_event_read` permission.

Calendar is in AgentMail Labs, available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`) but not yet
in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

403.description:
The organization does not have calendar access (it has not joined AgentMail Labs), or the API
key lacks the required calendar permission.

post.description:
Creates a one-off or recurring event on the inbox's calendar. Times are wall-clock values in
`timezone` (the calendar's default time zone if omitted); the response also gives each
boundary as a UTC instant in `start_at` and `end_at`.

`calendar.event.created` is sent once the event is stored, then `calendar.event.starting`
and `calendar.event.ending` as each date begins and ends. With `send_invites: true` the
inbox also emails an invitation to every attendee.

Pass `client_id` to make retries safe: repeating the request with the same `client_id` and
body returns the original event with status `200` instead of `201`, for as long as the event
exists.

With `send_invites: true`, each attendee counts as one send against the organization, pod
and inbox send limits, charged before the event is stored. An over-limit request returns
`429` `rate_limit_exceeded` and creates nothing. A replay of an earlier create is not
charged again.

The event's `etag` is the value to send in `If-Match` to make a later update or delete
conditional. Requires the `calendar_event_create` permission.

Calendar is in AgentMail Labs, available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`) but not yet
in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

The organization does not have calendar access (it has not joined AgentMail Labs), or the API
key lacks the required calendar permission.

413.description: The request body is too large (8 KB for calendar settings, 128 KB for events).

429.description:
Too many requests, or the invitation emails this request would send exceed an organization,
pod or inbox send limit. Nothing was changed. Honor the `Retry-After` header when present.

get.description:
Lists every date on the calendar in a time window, ordered by start time: one-off events,
and recurring events expanded into their individual dates, with cancelled dates left out.
Use it to answer "what is on the calendar".

The window defaults to now through 90 days from now and can be at most 366 days. Items omit
`description`, `metadata` and `attendees`; get an event by ID for the full object. An item
the inbox is invited to still carries `response_status`, so `needs_action` marks an
invitation waiting for a reply. Dates of
recurring events appear only up to about 90 days from now; use List Event Instances for a
recurring event's later dates. While a recurring event's dates are being regenerated after a
schedule change, which takes a few seconds, the agenda can briefly leave out some of them;
dates that have already started or ended stay as they ran.

moments earlier by a few seconds. Pass `consistency=primary` to read your own change right
away. Requires the `calendar_event_read` permission.

Gets an event by its UUID, or one date of a recurring event by its dated ID
(`<uuid>_<slot>`). A dated ID returns the date as it currently stands, including any edit
to it, with `kind: instance`.

The response's `etag` (also the `ETag` header) is the value to send in `If-Match` to make an
update, delete or response to this event or date conditional. Treat it as opaque.

Reads can trail a change made moments earlier by a few seconds; pass `consistency=primary`
to read the latest state of an event or a date. A date that has already started or ended
reads back as it ran, even if a later change to the series no longer produces it. Requires
the `calendar_event_read` permission.

in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

patch.description:
Updates an event. Send only the fields to change. To make the update conditional, send the
event's current `etag` in `If-Match`: a stale value returns `412`. Without `If-Match` the
update applies to the event as it is; a change that lands while it runs returns `409`
`race_condition`, so retry. Send `If-Match` when replacing `attendees`, so you don't
overwrite a response that arrived in the meantime.

- **One-off or series UUID:** changes the event itself. For a series, the change applies to
  every date that has not been edited individually.
- **Dated ID (`<uuid>_<slot>`):** changes one date (`mode=single`, the default) or that date
  and every later date (`mode=future`). `all_day`, `timezone` and `recurrence` cannot be sent
  for a dated ID.

Once a date has started, its start can no longer change (409 `event_already_started`), but
its end and status can; for a one-off or series UUID, send the unchanged `start` with the new
`end`. Once it has ended, only `title`, `description`, `location`,
`metadata` and `attendees` can change. During the few seconds a date is starting, schedule
changes return 409 `event_starting`; retry shortly.

Sends `calendar.event.updated`. With `send_invites: true` the organizer inbox also emails the
updated invitation to every attendee. Requires the `calendar_event_update` permission.

Emailing attendees counts one send per attendee against the organization, pod and inbox
send limits, charged before the change is saved; an over-limit request returns `429`
`rate_limit_exceeded` and changes nothing.

in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

delete.description:
Deletes an event, or cancels dates of a recurring event.

- **One-off or series UUID:** deletes the event and every date of it. The event disappears
  from reads immediately and is removed in the background; the response is `202` with a
  `deletion_id`. A retry returns the same `deletion_id` while removal runs (send the same
  `Idempotency-Key`, or none and the same `send_invites`); once it has finished, the event
  no longer exists and a retry returns `404`. No `calendar.event.starting` or
  `calendar.event.ending` webhook is sent for the event after the delete is accepted.
- **Dated ID (`<uuid>_<slot>`):** cancels that date (`mode=single`, the default) or that date
  and every later date (`mode=future`). Returns `202` with the cancelled date. A `mode=future`
  delete from the first date deletes the whole series and returns a `deletion_id` instead.
  A date that is already running still gets its `calendar.event.ending`.

`calendar.event.updated` with the cancelled date. With `send_invites=true` the organizer
inbox also emails a cancellation to every attendee. Requires the `calendar_event_delete`
permission. To make the delete conditional, send the current `etag` in `If-Match`.

Emailing cancellations counts one send per attendee against the organization, pod and inbox
send limits, charged before the delete; an over-limit request returns `429`
`rate_limit_exceeded` and deletes nothing.

in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`). Organizations that have not joined Labs receive a `403`.

`Authentication-Results` header (RFC 8601). `none` means there was nothing to evaluate
(Amazon SES calls this GRAY): no SPF record for the envelope MAIL FROM domain, no DKIM
signature to check, or no DMARC record for the From domain.

`pass` or `fail`.

dmarc_domain.description: From domain the `dmarc` verdict is about (`header.from`).

arc_sealer.description:
Domain of the trusted forwarder whose ARC seal the verdicts were taken from, such as
`google.com`. Present only on forwarded mail, and only beside at least one verdict.

messages_MessageAuthenticationResults.description:
Per-mechanism SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verdicts for a received message, each with the domain it
is about, kept only where they speak for the sender's From identity. A verdict that could
not be computed is absent, so the field can be `{}`. The field is absent on sent messages
and on messages received before 2026-09-09; the `*_domain` and `arc_sealer` keys appear on
messages received after they were introduced.

The verdicts are the ones Amazon SES computed when the message reached AgentMail, with one
exception. Forwarded mail fails DMARC at the receiving hop by construction. When AgentMail
delivers a forwarded message as authenticated because a trusted forwarder (such as Google or
Microsoft) sealed a valid ARC chain vouching for the original, the field reports the
verdicts that forwarder recorded for the original message, and `arc_sealer` names it.

- `spf` is about the envelope MAIL FROM (Return-Path) domain, named in `spf_domain`. It is
  present only when that domain is aligned with the sender's domain (the From mailbox, or
  the Sender header when From spans domains), meaning the two share an organizational
  domain: `mail.example.com` is aligned with `example.com`. An unaligned SPF result is
  withheld whatever its value.
- `dkim` is the DKIM verdict, and `dkim_domain` the signing domain (the `d=` tag). On
  directly received mail the domain is named only when every DKIM signature on the message
  is from the same domain; a message signed by more than one domain (a sender and its email
  provider, for instance) keeps the verdict and omits the domain. `dkim_domain` is the
  signing domain as written, so compare it with the From domain before relying on it.
- `dmarc` is the DMARC verdict for the From domain, named in `dmarc_domain`.
- `dkim` and `dmarc` are withheld when the From list spans more than one domain or could not
  be fully parsed.
- On forwarded mail each sealed verdict is reported only when the domain the forwarder
  recorded it for matches the message's current From domain. If the forwarder rewrote From,
  or vouched for nothing, the field is `{}`.

The `unauthenticated` label, not this field, is AgentMail's acceptance decision, and it uses
a looser rule, so the two can disagree: a single-From message whose only pass is an
unaligned envelope SPF is delivered without the label while this field shows no pass. Use
the label to tell whether AgentMail accepted the message as legitimate, and this field to
see which domain each mechanism authenticated. Do not reject mail on `dmarc: fail` alone.

drafts_DraftBcc.description: Addresses of BCC recipients. In format `username@domain.com` or `Display Name <username@domain.com>`.
drafts_DraftBcc.title: DraftBcc

drafts_DraftInReplyTo.description: ID of message being replied to.
drafts_DraftInReplyTo.title: DraftInReplyTo

drafts_DraftSendAt.description: Time at which to schedule send draft.
drafts_DraftSendAt.title: DraftSendAt

drafts_DraftUpdatedAt.description: Time at which draft was last updated.
drafts_DraftUpdatedAt.title: DraftUpdatedAt

drafts_DraftReplyTo.description: Reply-to addresses. In format `username@domain.com` or `Display Name <username@domain.com>`.
drafts_DraftReplyTo.title: DraftReplyTo

references.description: IDs of previous messages in thread.

created_at.description: Time at which draft was created.

drafts_DraftReplyAll.description: Reply to all recipients of the original message.
drafts_DraftReplyAll.title: DraftReplyAll

drafts_CreateDraftRequest.description:
Body for creating a draft. Supports plain, reply, reply-all, and forward
drafts:

- **Plain draft:** supply `to`, `subject`, `text`, etc.
- **Reply:** set `in_reply_to` to a message ID. Recipients, subject, and
  threading are derived from that message. Set `reply_all` to address the
  whole thread (you then cannot also pass `to`, `cc`, or `bcc`).
- **Forward:** set `forward_of` to a message ID. The subject and threading
  are derived from the source message, whose body and attachments are
  merged in at send time.

`in_reply_to` and `forward_of` are mutually exclusive, and reading the
referenced message requires `message_read` permission.
drafts_CreateDraftRequest.title: CreateDraftRequest

add_attachments.description: Attachments to add to the draft.

remove_attachments.description: IDs of attachments to remove from the draft.

add_labels.description: Label or labels to add to the draft.

remove_labels.description: Label or labels to remove from the draft.

drafts_UpdateDraftRequest.description:
Edit fields on an existing draft. A draft's kind (plain, reply, or forward)
is fixed at creation and cannot be changed here. Omitting a field leaves it
unchanged; passing `null` (or `[]` for a recipient field) clears it. Pass
`send_at` to schedule or reschedule the draft, or `null` to un-schedule it.
drafts_UpdateDraftRequest.title: UpdateDraftRequest

events_EventTypes.description: Event types for which to send events.
events_EventTypes.title: EventTypes

events_PodIds.description: Pods for which to send events.
events_PodIds.title: PodIds

events_InboxIds.description: Inboxes for which to send events.
events_InboxIds.title: InboxIds

pod_id.description:
ID of the pod the webhook belongs to: the pod it was created in, or the pod of the inbox it
belongs to. Absent for an organization webhook and on some inbox webhooks. This is not the
list of pods it receives events for; see `pod_ids`.

inbox_id.description:
ID of the inbox the webhook belongs to, if it was created for an inbox. This is not the list
of inboxes it receives events for; see `inbox_ids`.

enabled.description:
Whether the webhook is enabled. It becomes false when you disable it, and also when deliveries to
the URL have failed for 5 days, in which case AgentMail sends no notification. Re-enable it with
update and `enabled` set to true.

updated_at.description: Time at which webhook was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which webhook was created.

header_names.description: Names of the custom delivery headers configured for this webhook. Header values are never returned.

webhooks_CreateWebhookEventTypes.description:
Full list of event types this webhook should receive. Required: omitting it or sending an empty array
returns a `400`, and there is no "all events" default. Send every type you want in this array (not
incremental). See [Webhooks overview](https://docs.agentmail.to/webhooks-overview)
for spam, blocked, and unauthenticated events and required permissions.
webhooks_CreateWebhookEventTypes.title: CreateWebhookEventTypes

webhooks_WebhookHeaders.description:
Custom HTTP headers to include with every delivery to this webhook. Header values are write-only:
AgentMail never returns them from webhook read endpoints. The map must contain at least one entry
when provided, and every name and value must be a valid HTTP header.
webhooks_WebhookHeaders.title: WebhookHeaders

webhooks_CreateInboxWebhookRequest.description:
Create a webhook scoped to an inbox. The inbox comes from the path, so `inbox_ids` and `pod_ids`
are not accepted.
webhooks_CreateInboxWebhookRequest.title: CreateInboxWebhookRequest

webhooks_UpdateWebhookEventTypes.description:
When you send a non-empty list, it replaces the webhook's subscribed event types in full (the same
"set the list" behavior as create). It is not a merge or diff: include every event type you want after
the update. Sending a one-element array means the webhook will only receive that one type afterward.
Omit this field to leave event types unchanged. An empty array is rejected with a `400`: a webhook
always has at least one event type. Subscribing to `message.received.spam`, `message.received.blocked`, or
`message.received.unauthenticated` requires the matching label permission on the API key.
webhooks_UpdateWebhookEventTypes.title: UpdateWebhookEventTypes

enabled.description:
Set to true to re-enable a webhook that was disabled after repeated failed deliveries, or false
to disable it. AgentMail does not notify you when a webhook is disabled automatically; check this
field when you get or list webhooks. Events that occurred while the webhook was disabled are not
redelivered. Re-enabling requires the read permission for every restricted event type the webhook
subscribes to: `label_spam_read`, `label_blocked_read`, or `label_unauthenticated_read` for the
received variants, `message_read` for `message.security.*`, and `calendar_event_read` for
`calendar.event.*`. A webhook with no event type filter is checked against all of them.

webhooks_UpdateInboxWebhookRequest.description:
Update an inbox-scoped webhook. It is fixed to its inbox, so only `event_types` and `enabled` can
change.
webhooks_UpdateInboxWebhookRequest.title: UpdateInboxWebhookRequest

remove_headers.description: Names of custom delivery headers to remove.

webhooks_UpdateWebhookHeadersRequest.description:
Set, replace, or remove custom delivery headers. Provide at least one of `headers` or
`remove_headers`. A header cannot be set and removed in the same request, regardless of casing.
webhooks_UpdateWebhookHeadersRequest.title: UpdateWebhookHeadersRequest

webhooks_polling_PollingClientId.description:
Required. Idempotency key of the subscription: creating again with the same `client_id` through the
same route returns the existing subscription with a fresh token instead of a second subscription, so a
restarted agent resumes where it left off. Also accepted in place of `webhook_id` on get and delete.
webhooks_polling_PollingClientId.title: PollingClientId

pod_id.description:
ID of the pod the subscription belongs to: the pod it was created in, or the pod of the inbox it
belongs to. Absent for an organization subscription. This is not the list of pods it receives
events for; see `pod_ids`.

inbox_id.description:
ID of the inbox the subscription belongs to, if it was created for an inbox. This is not the
list of inboxes it receives events for; see `inbox_ids`.

updated_at.description: Time at which the subscription was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which the subscription was created.

webhooks_polling_PollingWebhook.description:
A subscription the agent polls for events instead of receiving them at a URL. Same event types,
channels (pods and inboxes) and permissions as a webhook; no public endpoint is needed.
webhooks_polling_PollingWebhook.title: PollingWebhook

polling_webhooks.description:
Ordered by `created_at` descending. Lists the subscriptions created through this route
(organization, pod, or inbox); subscriptions created through a pod or inbox route are listed
through that route.

webhooks_polling_CreateInboxPollingWebho.description:
Create a polling webhook scoped to an inbox. The inbox comes from the path, so `inbox_ids` and
`pod_ids` are not accepted.
webhooks_polling_CreateInboxPollingWebho.title: CreateInboxPollingWebhookRequest

webhooks_polling_PollingToken.description:
Credential for reading this subscription's events. Hand it to the Svix AutoConfig consumer
(`AutoConfigConsumer` in the `svix` package for TypeScript and Python): `receive` returns the events
queued since your last commit, `commit` marks them as processed. Returned by create only and never
readable afterward. Create again with the same `client_id` to get a new token; the previous one stops
working immediately.
webhooks_polling_PollingToken.title: PollingToken

pod_id.description:
ID of the pod the subscription belongs to: the pod it was created in, or the pod of the inbox it
belongs to. Absent for an organization subscription. This is not the list of pods it receives
events for; see `pod_ids`.

inbox_id.description:
ID of the inbox the subscription belongs to, if it was created for an inbox. This is not the
list of inboxes it receives events for; see `inbox_ids`.

updated_at.description: Time at which the subscription was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which the subscription was created.

webhooks_polling_CreatePollingWebhookRes.description: The subscription plus the one-time `token` that reads it.
webhooks_polling_CreatePollingWebhookRes.title: CreatePollingWebhookResponse

lists_EntryType.description: Whether the entry is an email address or domain.
lists_EntryType.title: EntryType

entry.description: Email address or domain of list entry.

created_at.description: Time at which entry was created.

read_only.description: Whether the entry is read-only and cannot be deleted via the API.

inbox_id.description: ID of inbox, if entry is inbox-scoped.

entry.description: Email address or domain to add.

metrics_MetricEventTypes.description: List of metric event types to query.
metrics_MetricEventTypes.title: MetricEventTypes

metrics_Period.description: Size of each time bucket as a whole number of seconds, between 1 and 86400.
metrics_Period.title: Period

metrics_MetricLimit.description: Limit on number of buckets to return.
metrics_MetricLimit.title: MetricLimit

count.description: Count of events in the bucket.

metrics_UsageType.description:
Type of usage metric. Inbox-scoped queries carry `storage_bytes`,
`message_count`, and `thread_count`; pod-scoped queries add `inbox_count`
and `domain_count`; organization-scoped queries add `pod_count`.
metrics_UsageType.title: UsageType

metrics_UsageTypes.description: List of usage metric types to query. Omit to query every type valid for the scope.
metrics_UsageTypes.title: UsageTypes

value.description: Cumulative value of the usage metric at the timestamp.

metrics_QueryUsageResponse.description: Cumulative usage series grouped by usage type.
metrics_QueryUsageResponse.title: QueryUsageResponse

metrics_RateType.description:
Type of rate. `bounce` is bounced messages divided by messages sent,
counting permanent and transient bounces; `complaint` is spam complaints
divided by messages sent.
metrics_RateType.title: RateType

metrics_RateTypes.description: List of rate types to query. Omit to query both.
metrics_RateTypes.title: RateTypes

metrics_RatePeriod.description:
How often a point is sampled, as a whole number of seconds between 60
and 86400. Defaults to 3600 (one point per hour).
metrics_RatePeriod.title: RatePeriod

metrics_Window.description:
How far back each point looks, as a whole number of seconds. Must be a
whole multiple of `period`, at most 30 days (2592000). Defaults to 86400
(a rolling 24-hour rate).
metrics_Window.title: Window

timestamp.description: End of the window the point covers; the window is the `window` seconds before it.

rate.description:
Bounced or complained messages divided by messages sent over the
window, as a fraction (0.05 is 5%). Null when nothing was sent in
the window.

sent.description: Messages sent in the window, counted per recipient.

metrics_QueryRatesResponse.description: Rate series grouped by rate type.
metrics_QueryRatesResponse.title: QueryRatesResponse

inboxEvents_InboxEventType.description:
Type of inbox event. Wire format is dot.case to match the
convention used by webhook events (`message.received`,
`domain.verified`, etc. in events.yml). Pre-2026-04 these were
`label_added`/`label_removed` (snake_case). The Fern enum's `name`
field stays uppercase-snake (Fern convention); only the wire
`value` changed.
inboxEvents_InboxEventType.title: InboxEventType

event_at.description: Time at which the event occurred.

created_at.description: Time at which the event was recorded.

apiKeys_PodScopeId.description: Pod ID the api key is scoped to. If set, the key can only access resources within this pod.
apiKeys_PodScopeId.title: PodScopeId

apiKeys_InboxScopeId.description: Inbox ID the api key is scoped to. If set, the key can only access resources within this inbox.
apiKeys_InboxScopeId.title: InboxScopeId

apiKeys_UsedAt.description: Time at which api key was last used.
apiKeys_UsedAt.title: UsedAt

message_read.description: Read messages. Also required to read threads.

message_reply.description: Reply and reply-all when the request is signed with a registered public key. Bearer keys reply with `message_send`.

message_update.description: Update message labels. Also required to update threads.

message_delete.description: Delete messages. Also required to delete threads.

agent_armor_release.description:
Release mail Agent Armor holds for review. Opt-in: no key has it unless it was granted explicitly, even one
without a `permissions` object. See [Permissions](/permissions#agent-armor).

app_connect.description:
Sign in to apps as an inbox: connect an app, authorize an inbox, and mint the
sign-in keys. Omitted on a new bearer key means false, whatever else the key holds.

app_share_owner.description:
Share the organization owner's name and email with apps at sign-in. One permission
for both values.

account_update.description:
Update accounts: disable or re-enable an inbox's sign-in at an app. Reading accounts
needs only `inbox_read`.

calendar_event_read.description: Read calendar events, and receive `calendar.event.*` webhook and WebSocket events.

calendar_event_update.description: Update calendar events and respond to invitations.

apiKeys_ApiKeyPermissions.description: Granular permissions for the API key. When ommitted all permissions are granted. Otherwise, only permissions set to true are granted.
apiKeys_ApiKeyPermissions.title: ApiKeyPermissions

apiKeys_CreatedAt.description: Time at which api key was created.
apiKeys_CreatedAt.title: CreatedAt

apiKeys_UpdatedAt.description: Time at which api key was last updated.
apiKeys_UpdatedAt.title: UpdatedAt

apiKeys_ExpiresAt.description: Time at which api key expires. Omitted when it does not expire.
apiKeys_ExpiresAt.title: ExpiresAt

apiKeys_BearerApiKey.description: An API key presented as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
apiKeys_BearerApiKey.title: BearerApiKey

apiKeys_PublicKeyClientId.description:
Caller-chosen alias for a public key, unique within the organization and
reusable after deletion. Accepted in place of `api_key_id` on get, update,
and delete. Registration is idempotent on it: the same alias returns the
existing key, a conflicting one returns `409`. URL-safe; no slash or `@`.
apiKeys_PublicKeyClientId.title: PublicKeyClientId

apiKeys_PublicJwkCoordinate.description: A 32-byte P-256 coordinate encoded as unpadded base64url.
apiKeys_PublicJwkCoordinate.title: PublicJwkCoordinate

apiKeys_PublicJwk.description:
A public P-256 JWK. The object accepts exactly `kty`, `crv`, `x`, and `y`.
Private key material such as `d`, embedded key IDs, and all other members
are rejected. The server also rejects coordinates that are not a point on
P-256.
apiKeys_PublicJwk.title: PublicJwk

fingerprint.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint encoded as unpadded base64url.

apiKeys_PublicKeyMaterial.description: Registered public key material and its server-computed RFC 7638 thumbprint.
apiKeys_PublicKeyMaterial.title: PublicKeyMaterial

apiKeys_PublicKeyStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a sign-in key: `pending` until the client finishes
creating it on the AgentID page, `active` once it can sign in as the
inbox. Absent on a registered key.
apiKeys_PublicKeyStatus.title: PublicKeyStatus

apiKeys_ApiKeyCreator.description: The bearer API key that created the credential. Provenance only; the credential outlives it.
apiKeys_ApiKeyCreator.title: ApiKeyCreator

apiKeys_PublicKeyCredential.description:
An AgentID sign-in credential, scoped like a bearer key; `api_key_id` is
the JWS `kid`. A sign-in key carries `status`, gains `public_key` once
the client has proved it, expires 30 days after
activation, and carries exactly `app_connect` and
`app_share_owner`, snapshotted from the bearer key that created it
and enforced from the key itself.
apiKeys_PublicKeyCredential.title: PublicKeyCredential

apiKeys_ApiKey.description:
One credential of any family. `type` is `bearer` or `public_key`. A
public key carrying `status` is a sign-in key; one without it is a
registered signing key.
apiKeys_ApiKey.title: ApiKey

api_keys.description:
Every credential family, ordered by `created_at`. `type` restricts
to one family.

apiKeys_CreateBearerApiKeyRequest.description:
`expires_at` must be in the future and is immutable once the key exists.
Omitted, the new key inherits the authenticating key's expiry, and never
expires only when that key never does. A key cannot create one that
outlives it: an `expires_at` later than the authenticating key's own
returns `403`.
apiKeys_CreateBearerApiKeyRequest.title: CreateBearerApiKeyRequest

apiKeys_CreatePublicKeyRequest.description:
Registers a public P-256 JWK at the route's scope. `type` and
`api_key_id` are server-owned. `name` defaults to
`AgentID key {first eight fingerprint characters}`; `permissions`
defaults to the registering key's, and only grants it holds may be
true; `expires_at` defaults to the registering key's expiry and is
independent of that key afterward.
apiKeys_CreatePublicKeyRequest.title: CreatePublicKeyRequest

apiKeys_CreateApiKeyRequest.description:
A body with `public_key` registers a public-key credential; any other
body mints a bearer key.
apiKeys_CreateApiKeyRequest.title: CreateApiKeyRequest

apiKeys_CreateApiKeyResult.description: The secret-bearing bearer key, or the registered public key without any secret.
apiKeys_CreateApiKeyResult.title: CreateApiKeyResult

apiKeys_UpdateApiKeyRequest.description:
Rename a credential or change its permissions. Key material, type,
scope, and expiry are immutable.
apiKeys_UpdateApiKeyRequest.title: UpdateApiKeyRequest

accounts_AccountStatus.description:
`disabled` refuses every new sign-in for the account until it is
re-enabled. Access tokens already issued are not revoked.
accounts_AccountStatus.title: AccountStatus

first_signed_in_at.description: Time of first sign-in at app.

last_signed_in_at.description: Time of most recent sign-in at app.

status.description: Present only while the account is disabled. Absent means the inbox may sign in.

disabled_at.description: Time at which the account was disabled. Present only while `status` is `disabled`.

accounts_Account.description: One inbox signed in at one app.
accounts_Account.title: Account

calendar_CalendarConsistency.description:
Read consistency. `eventual` (default) reads from the region that serves your request and may
lag a write made moments earlier by up to a few seconds. `primary` reads from the primary region
and always reflects every completed write.
calendar_CalendarConsistency.title: CalendarConsistency

calendar_IanaTimezone.description:
Canonical IANA time zone name, for example `America/New_York`, `Europe/London` or `UTC`.
Abbreviations such as `PST`, Windows names such as `Pacific Standard Time`, and spellings that
differ from the canonical name are rejected.
calendar_IanaTimezone.title: IanaTimezone

timezone.description:
Default time zone for events created without a `timezone`. Defaults to `UTC`. Changing it
does not move existing events.

event_count.description: Number of one-off and recurring events on the calendar. Each recurring event counts once.

created_at.description: Time at which the calendar was created. The calendar exists from the moment the inbox does, so this is the inbox's creation time.

updated_at.description: Time at which the calendar was last updated.

etag.description:
The calendar's current version, also sent as the `ETag` response header. Send it in
`If-Match` to make an update conditional.

calendar_Calendar.description:
An inbox's calendar. Every inbox has exactly one calendar; it exists from the moment the inbox
does and is deleted with it.
calendar_Calendar.title: Calendar

calendar_CalendarLimit.description: Maximum number of events to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.
calendar_CalendarLimit.title: CalendarLimit

calendar_CalendarEventId.description:
ID of a calendar event. A one-off or recurring event is addressed by its UUID. One date of a
recurring event is addressed by a dated ID, `<uuid>_<slot>`: `<uuid>_t20261015T090000` for a
timed date (the original wall-clock start in the event's time zone) or `<uuid>_d20261015` for an
all-day date. Dated IDs are stable: moving a date keeps its original ID.
calendar_CalendarEventId.title: CalendarEventId

calendar_CalendarEventKind.description:
What the event object represents.

- `single`: a one-off event, addressed by its UUID.
- `series`: the definition of a recurring event, addressed by its UUID. It carries
  `recurrence`; `start` and `end` describe its first date.
- `instance`: one date of a recurring event, addressed by its dated ID. It carries `series_id`,
  `original_start` and `is_exception`.
calendar_CalendarEventKind.title: CalendarEventKind

calendar_WallTime.description:
A local wall-clock time without an offset, interpreted in the event's `timezone`.
Timed events use `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` (for example `2026-10-15T09:00:00`). All-day events use
`YYYY-MM-DD`. Years must be between 1900 and 9999.
calendar_WallTime.title: WallTime

calendar_CalendarEventStatus.description:
Status of the event. A `cancelled` event or date stays readable but sends no
`calendar.event.starting` or `calendar.event.ending` webhooks (cancelling a date that is
already running still sends its `calendar.event.ending`). A date cancelled by deleting its
dated ID is removed from the series instead, so reading it can return `404` or `410`.
calendar_CalendarEventStatus.title: CalendarEventStatus

calendar_DurationMode.description:
How the event's length is kept when a date crosses a daylight-saving change.

- `exact`: the event lasts the same elapsed time. Default for one-off timed events.
- `nominal`: the event keeps its wall-clock end time (a 09:00 to 10:00 meeting stays 09:00 to
  10:00 local time). Default for recurring timed events.

All-day events are always `nominal`.
calendar_DurationMode.title: DurationMode

calendar_RecurrencePeriod.description: An extra date (RDATE) given as a period. Specify exactly one of `end` or `duration`.
calendar_RecurrencePeriod.title: RecurrencePeriod

calendar_RecurrenceDate.description: A wall-clock date or date-time, or (timed events only) a period.
calendar_RecurrenceDate.title: RecurrenceDate

rule.description: Normalized RRULE body, without the `RRULE:` prefix.

truncate_before.description:
Set when the series was ended with a `mode=future` delete: no date starting at or after
this wall-clock time occurs.

calendar_Recurrence.description: The recurrence of a series, as stored.
calendar_Recurrence.title: Recurrence

calendar_AttendeeStatus.description: The attendee's response to the invitation.
calendar_AttendeeStatus.title: AttendeeStatus

calendar_AttendeeRole.description: Whether the attendee's presence is required.
calendar_AttendeeRole.title: AttendeeRole

email.description: Email address of the attendee. Stored in lowercase. Must be unique within the event.

name.description: Display name of the attendee. At most 256 characters.

comment.description:
Comment the attendee sent with their response. At most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes; on create or
update, a longer comment is dropped rather than rejected.

responded_at.description: Time at which the attendee last responded.

calendar_CalendarEventSource.title: CalendarEventSource

calendar_ResourceRevision.description:
Revision of the resource. It increases on every change. The resource's `etag` is
`"rv-<resource_revision>"`.
calendar_ResourceRevision.title: ResourceRevision

series_id.description: For `instance` events, the UUID of the series this date belongs to.

original_start.description: For `instance` events, the date's start as the series rule generated it, before any edit.

original_start_at.description: For `instance` events, `original_start` as a UTC instant.

is_exception.description: For `instance` events, `true` when this date was edited or moved, individually or by a `mode=future` change.

description.description: Description of the event. Omitted from agenda and instance list items.

metadata.description: Your own JSON value for the event, usually an object. Never sent to attendees. Omitted from agenda and instance list items.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event.

start.description: Local start time in `timezone`. For all-day events, the first day.

end.description: Local end time in `timezone`. For all-day events, the last day (inclusive).

duration_value.description: Length of the event, in milliseconds for timed events and in days for all-day events.

start_at.description: Start as a UTC instant. This is when `calendar.event.starting` is due.

end_at.description: End as a UTC instant. This is when `calendar.event.ending` is due.

attendees.description: Attendees of the event. Omitted from agenda and instance list items; `attendee_count` is always present.

response_status.description:
The inbox's own response: the `status` of its entry in `attendees`. Present only on events
the inbox can respond to: `email` events with an `organizer_email` and an
`origin_message_id` that list the inbox as an attendee. Included on agenda and instance list
items, which omit `attendees`. `needs_action` means the invitation is waiting for a reply.

uid.description: iCalendar UID of the event. Invitations about this event carry the same UID.

sequence.description:
iCalendar SEQUENCE number. It increases when a change to a one-off or series event affects
what attendees see (time, status, title, description, location, recurrence or attendees).
A change to a dated event increases it only when the change is sent with `send_invites`.

organizer_email.description: Email address of the organizer. For `api` events, the inbox.

origin_message_id.description: For `email` events, the ID of the message whose invitation last created or updated the event.

resource_revision.description:
Present on `single` and `series` events, except agenda items and
`calendar.event.starting` and `calendar.event.ending` payloads, which omit it.

created_at.description: Time at which the event (or, for a date, the definition governing it) was created.

updated_at.description: Time at which the event (or, for a date, the definition governing it) was last updated.

etag.description:
The event's or date's current version, also sent as the `ETag` response header. Send it in
`If-Match` to make an update, delete or response conditional. Present on Get, Create,
Update, Delete and Respond responses; list items and webhooks omit it. Treat it as opaque:
a dated event's `etag` (`"occ-..."`) is not derived from `resource_revision`.

calendar_CalendarEvent.description:
A calendar event. The same shape is used by every response, list item and webhook. `kind` says
whether it is a one-off event, the definition of a recurring series, or one date of a series.
calendar_CalendarEvent.title: CalendarEvent

events.description:
On List Events, ordered by `updated_at` descending. On Get Agenda and List Event Instances,
ordered by `start_at` ascending.

calendar_WindowAfter.description:
Start of the window, as a UTC timestamp ending in `Z` (an offset such as `-04:00` is
rejected). Defaults to now. The window between `after` and `before` can be at most 366 days.
calendar_WindowAfter.title: WindowAfter

calendar_WindowBefore.description:
End of the window, as a UTC timestamp ending in `Z` (an offset such as `-04:00` is rejected).
Defaults to 90 days after `after`. The window between `after` and `before` can be at most 366
days.
calendar_WindowBefore.title: WindowBefore

calendar_IncludeOverlapping.description:
When `true` (default), include events that started before `after` but are still running at
`after`. When `false`, include only events that start inside the window.
calendar_IncludeOverlapping.title: IncludeOverlapping

rule.description:
RFC 5545 RRULE body, with or without the `RRULE:` prefix, for example
`FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR` or `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR;COUNT=12`. Supported parts: `FREQ`,
`INTERVAL` (1 to 366), `COUNT` (1 to 10,000), `UNTIL` (`YYYYMMDD` for all-day events,
`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` for timed events),
`WKST`, `BYMONTH`, `BYWEEKNO`, `BYYEARDAY`, `BYMONTHDAY`, `BYDAY`, `BYHOUR`, `BYMINUTE`,
`BYSECOND` and `BYSETPOS`. `COUNT` and `UNTIL` are mutually exclusive. The rule is stored in
a normalized form, so a response can differ textually from what you sent. At most 512
characters after normalization.

exdates.description:
Dates to skip, matching the original start of a date: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` for timed events,
`YYYY-MM-DD` for all-day events. At most 366.

rdates.description:
Extra dates to add. Timed events take date-times or periods; all-day events take dates. At
most 100.

calendar_RecurrenceInput.description:
Repeats the event. `rule` is an RFC 5545 RRULE, evaluated in the event's `timezone` from the
event's `start`. Each date keeps its wall-clock time across daylight-saving changes.
calendar_RecurrenceInput.title: RecurrenceInput

client_id.description:
Your idempotency key for this create. Retrying with the same `client_id` and the same body
returns the original event with `200` instead of creating a second one, for as long as the
event exists (`404` once it has been deleted). Reusing it with a different body is a `409`
`idempotency_conflict`.

title.description: Title of the event. 1 to 1,000 characters.

description.description: Description of the event. At most 65,536 bytes.

location.description: Location of the event. At most 1,024 characters.

metadata.description: Your own JSON value (usually an object), returned on reads and in webhooks (except agenda and instance list items, and the webhook for a date cancelled with `DELETE`). Never sent to attendees. At most 16,384 bytes serialized.

all_day.description: Set to `true` for an all-day event. Defaults to `false`.

start.description:
Local start time in `timezone`: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` for timed events, `YYYY-MM-DD` for
all-day events. For a recurring event, this is the first date.

end.description:
Local end time in `timezone`, in the same format as `start`. For timed events it must be
after `start`; for all-day events it is the last day (inclusive) and can equal `start`.
One-off events can last up to 366 days; each date of a recurring event up to 31 days.

timezone.description: Time zone of `start` and `end`. Defaults to the calendar's `timezone`.

duration_mode.description: Timed events only. Defaults to `exact` for one-off events and `nominal` for recurring events.

attendees.description: Attendees of the event. At most 100.

send_invites.description:
When `true`, the inbox emails an invitation (iCalendar `REQUEST`) to every attendee. Defaults
to `false`.

calendar_OperationId.description:
ID of the change this request made. The `calendar.event.created`, `calendar.event.updated`,
`calendar.event.deleted` or `calendar.event.responded` webhook for the change carries the same
value as its `event_id`, so you can match webhooks to your own requests.
calendar_OperationId.title: OperationId

calendar_InstanceMutationMode.title: InstanceMutationMode

calendar_DeletionId.description:
ID of an accepted deletion. While the event is being removed, retrying the same delete (with the
same `Idempotency-Key`, or none and the same `send_invites`) returns it again. Once removal has
finished, a retry returns `404`.
calendar_DeletionId.title: DeletionId

calendar_DeleteCalendarEventResponse.description:
Deleting a one-off or recurring event (or a `mode=future` delete that covers a whole series)
returns `deletion_id`. Deleting dates of a series returns the cancelled date as `event` with an
`operation_id`.
calendar_DeleteCalendarEventResponse.title: DeleteCalendarEventResponse

inbox_ids.description:
Inboxes for which to send events. A webhook can list at most 10 inboxes and pods combined;
more returns `403` with `limit_exceeded`.

pod_ids.description:
Pods for which to send events. A webhook can list at most 10 pods and inboxes combined; more returns
`403` with `limit_exceeded`. The webhook receives an event that matches any listed pod or inbox, so a
listed pod already covers every inbox in it.

enabled.description:
Set to true to re-enable a webhook that was disabled after repeated failed deliveries, or false
to disable it. AgentMail does not notify you when a webhook is disabled automatically; check this
field when you get or list webhooks. Events that occurred while the webhook was disabled are not
redelivered. Re-enabling requires the read permission for every restricted event type the webhook
subscribes to: `label_spam_read`, `label_blocked_read`, or `label_unauthenticated_read` for the
received variants, `message_read` for `message.security.*`, and `calendar_event_read` for
`calendar.event.*`. A webhook with no event type filter is checked against all of them.

add_inbox_ids.description:
Inbox IDs to subscribe to the webhook. This only adds to what the webhook receives: on a webhook
that covers its whole pod, it changes nothing. To receive only specific inboxes, create a webhook
with `inbox_ids` instead. The webhook can list at most 10 inboxes and pods combined after the
update.

remove_inbox_ids.description: Inbox IDs to unsubscribe from the webhook.

add_pod_ids.description:
Pod IDs to subscribe to the webhook. The webhook can list at most 10 pods and inboxes combined
after the update.

remove_pod_ids.description: Pod IDs to unsubscribe from the webhook.

pod_ids.description:
Pods for which to receive events. Maximum 10 channels (pods plus inboxes) per subscription. The
subscription receives an event that matches any listed pod or inbox, so a listed pod already
covers every inbox in it.

domains_FeedbackEnabled.description: Bounce and complaint notifications are sent to your inboxes.
domains_FeedbackEnabled.title: FeedbackEnabled

domains_InboundEnabled.description:
Receive email for this domain. Defaults to `true`. Set `false` for a send-only
domain: the apex MX record is not required and is omitted from `records`, so the
domain's existing email provider keeps receiving its mail. Inboxes on a send-only
domain can still send.
domains_InboundEnabled.title: InboundEnabled

domains_SubdomainsEnabled.description:
Allow inboxes on any subdomain of this domain. Adds a required wildcard MX
record (`*.<domain>`) to `records`.
domains_SubdomainsEnabled.title: SubdomainsEnabled

domains_TrackingEnabled.description:
Serve open tracking pixels from this domain. Adds a required `link.<domain>`
CNAME record to `records`, which must be published and verified before
`track_opens` can be used on a send.
domains_TrackingEnabled.title: TrackingEnabled

inbound_enabled.description: Absent on domains created before this field existed; those receive email.

updated_at.description: Time at which the domain was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which the domain was created.

domains_Status.description: The verification status of the domain.
domains_Status.title: Status

type.description: The type of the DNS record.

name.description: The name or host of the record.

status.description: The verification status of this specific record.

priority.description: The priority of the MX record.

reason.description: Why the record is INVALID, when known. `duplicate_records` means the expected value is present but extra records coexist at the same name; `value_mismatch` means a record exists but does not match the expected value.

Why the domain is not (yet) VERIFIED, when known. `dns_records_missing` / `dns_records_invalid` point at the DNS records. The `ses_*` values mean the records look right and sending-infrastructure validation has not converged: `ses_dkim_pending` / `ses_mail_from_pending` (still checking), `ses_dkim_temporary_failure` / `ses_mail_from_temporary_failure` (a transient error the infrastructure keeps retrying on its own — usually resolves without changes), `ses_dkim_failed` / `ses_mail_from_failed` (a terminal verdict; re-verify after fixing), `ses_dkim_not_started` / `ses_mail_from_not_started` (the attribute was never configured on the identity — re-verify to push it), and `ses_not_verified_for_sending`. Absent when VERIFIED.

inbound_enabled.description: Absent on domains created before this field existed; those receive email.

records.description:
A list of DNS records required to verify the domain. Includes the apex
MX record unless `inbound_enabled` is false, and a wildcard MX record
(`*.<domain>`) when `subdomains_enabled` is true.

updated_at.description: Time at which the domain was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which the domain was created.

allow_conflicting_provider.description:
Allow registration when the domain already has Google Workspace MX records.
Defaults to false; registration otherwise returns 422 when a conflicting
provider is detected.
This flag does not configure DNS or inbound routing. For shared Google
Workspace domains, follow the [Google Workspace guide](/google-workspace).
Only checked when `inbound_enabled` is true; a send-only domain skips the check.

domains_UpdateDomainRequest.description:
Provide at least one of `feedback_enabled`, `inbound_enabled`,
`subdomains_enabled`, or `tracking_enabled`. Omitted fields are left
unchanged; an empty body is rejected. Enabling `inbound_enabled` or
`subdomains_enabled` on a verified domain returns it to `PENDING` until the
newly required MX record (the apex MX, or the wildcard `*.<domain>`) is
published and verified.
domains_UpdateDomainRequest.title: UpdateDomainRequest

supported.description: Whether one-click setup is available for this domain. `false` means the domain's DNS provider does not support Domain Connect (or does not carry the AgentMail template yet) — add the domain's `records` manually instead.

provider_name.description: Display name of the domain's DNS provider, for the setup button label.

url.description: The signed Domain Connect apply URL. Open it in a browser: the domain owner signs in at their DNS provider, reviews the records, and approves — the provider writes them.

width.description: Suggested popup width from the provider, in pixels.

height.description: Suggested popup height from the provider, in pixels.

state.description: Opaque value echoed back on the provider's redirect. Store it before opening the URL and compare on return to tie the redirect to this request.

conflicting_provider.description: Set when the domain currently has another email provider's MX records (for example Google Workspace). Applying the template would replace them — warn before proceeding.

entry.description: Email address or domain of list entry.

created_at.description: Time at which entry was created.

read_only.description: Whether the entry is read-only and cannot be deleted via the API.

slug.description: Short name accepted in place of `app_id` by Get App, List App Accounts and Connect App. Set by AgentMail on apps in the catalog; renaming the app does not change it. Store `app_id`, the app's permanent ID.

updated_at.description: Time at which app was last updated.

categories.description: Kinds of app, up to 3. Omitted when the app sets none.

owner_signup_limit.description: Maximum number of accounts your organization may sign up at this app. Omitted when the app sets no limit. 0 means the app has paused new sign-ups; existing accounts keep signing in.

apps_App.description: An app an inbox can sign in to.
apps_App.title: App

apps_ConnectInboxId.description: Inbox to sign in as. Required unless the API key is scoped to an inbox.
apps_ConnectInboxId.title: ConnectInboxId

apps_MagicUrl.description: Single-use URL to open in the client that will hold the key.
apps_MagicUrl.title: MagicUrl

apps_ConnectAccepted.description: The pending sign-in key the client will activate. Poll Get API Key with `api_key_id` for `status`.
apps_ConnectAccepted.title: ConnectAccepted

accounts_UpdateAccountStatus.description:
Status to set. `disabled` stops the inbox from signing in at the
app; `enabled` re-enables it. An enabled account reads back with no
`status`.
accounts_UpdateAccountStatus.title: UpdateAccountStatus

accounts_UpdateAccountRequest.description:
Fields to change on the account. Fields you omit are left unchanged and
unknown fields are rejected. Expects at least one field; today that is
`status`.
accounts_UpdateAccountRequest.title: UpdateAccountRequest

created_at.description: Time at which pod was created.

Create a webhook scoped to a pod. The pod comes from the path, so `pod_ids` is not accepted.
Optionally pass `inbox_ids` to narrow the webhook to specific inboxes within the pod; omit to
receive events for the whole pod.
webhooks_CreatePodWebhookRequest.title: CreatePodWebhookRequest

to disable it. AgentMail does not notify you when a webhook is disabled automatically; check this
field when you get or list webhooks. Events that occurred while the webhook was disabled are not

received variants, `message_read` for `message.security.*`, and `calendar_event_read` for
`calendar.event.*`. A webhook with no event type filter is checked against all of them.

Inbox IDs to subscribe to the webhook. This only adds to what the webhook receives: on a webhook
that covers its whole pod, it changes nothing. To receive only specific inboxes, create a webhook

Update a pod-scoped webhook. You can adjust which inboxes within the pod it listens to, replace
its `event_types`, and set `enabled`, but not change the pod scope itself.
webhooks_UpdatePodWebhookRequest.title: UpdatePodWebhookRequest

webhooks_polling_CreatePodPollingWebhook.description:

suspended_at.description:
Time at which the organization was suspended. Absent when it is not suspended. A suspended
organization cannot send, but it still receives mail, its webhooks and WebSocket events still
fire, and API reads keep working. See [account_suspended](https://docs.agentmail.to/errors#account_suspended).

suspended_reason.description:
Why the organization is suspended, in a short machine-readable form such as `message.bounced`
or `message.complained`. Absent when it is not suspended. Email support@agentmail.cc to resolve
a suspension.

updated_at.description: Time at which organization was last updated.

created_at.description: Time at which organization was created.

organizations_Organization.description: Organization details with usage limits and counts.
organizations_Organization.title: Organization

enabled.description: Whether the organization is in AgentMail Labs.

enabled_at.description: Time at which the organization joined Labs. `null` when it is not in Labs.

available.description: Whether Labs is offered in this deployment. Labs is available in US production (`api.agentmail.to`), not yet in EU production (`api.agentmail.eu`).

organizations_OrganizationLabs.description: Whether the organization is in AgentMail Labs, and whether Labs is offered in this deployment.
organizations_OrganizationLabs.title: OrganizationLabs

auth_ScopeType.description: The scope tier the authenticated credential is bound to.
auth_ScopeType.title: ScopeType

scope_id.description:
ID of the most specific scope the credential is bound to.
Equals inbox_id when scope_type is inbox, pod_id when pod, organization_id when organization.

pod_id.description: ID of the pod the credential is scoped to. Present when scope_type is pod or inbox.

inbox_id.description: ID of the inbox the credential is scoped to. Present when scope_type is inbox.

api_key_id.description: ID of the API key used to authenticate. Absent for JWT and proxy credentials.

auth_Identity.description: Identity and scope of the authenticated credential.
auth_Identity.title: Identity

events_EventId.description:
ID of the event. It is the same on every retry and redelivery of the event and on every webhook
or WebSocket subscription that receives it, so use it to deduplicate. The format varies by event
type; treat it as an opaque string.
events_EventId.title: EventId

reply_to.description: Reply-to addresses. In format `username@domain.com` or `Display Name <username@domain.com>`.

body_url.description:
Pre-signed URL that downloads the stored body as a JSON object including `text`, `html`,
`extracted_text`, and `extracted_html`. Present only when the body is omitted from the event.
Valid until `body_expires_at`, one hour after the event was built. The body stays available
through the get message endpoint after the URL expires.

body_expires_at.description: Time at which `body_url` expires. Present only with `body_url`.

events_ReceivedMessage.description:
The received message. The body (`text`, `html`, `extracted_text`, and `extracted_html`) is included
inline only when it is small enough. Webhooks omit it when the stored body is larger than 64 KiB;
WebSocket events also omit it when the serialized event would be larger than 30 KiB. When the body
is omitted, `body_url` and `body_expires_at` are set instead.
events_ReceivedMessage.title: ReceivedMessage

events_MessageReceivedEvent.description: A message was received. Spam, blocked, and unauthenticated received-message events use the same payload shape with different `event_type` values.
events_MessageReceivedEvent.title: MessageReceivedEvent

reason.description: A short explanation of the verdict.

model.description: Identifies the Agent Armor release that produced the verdict. Opaque; it changes when Agent Armor is updated.

manual_override.description: Present on a `review` held in hold mode that someone released.

agentArmor_AgentArmorCompletedEventResul.description: The result in a `message.security.completed` or `message.security.review` event, which is always `complete`.
agentArmor_AgentArmorCompletedEventResul.title: AgentArmorCompletedEventResult

events_MessageSecurity.description: The message an Agent Armor result is for. Fetch the message for its content.
events_MessageSecurity.title: MessageSecurity

events_MessageSecurityCompletedEvent.description:
Agent Armor reached a verdict on a received message. Sent only in monitor mode, and only for `complete` results:
an `unavailable` result sends no event. Sent once per message and inbox; `event_id` is stable, so use it to
deduplicate. Not sent for messages labeled `spam`, `blocked`, `unauthenticated`, or `trash`: read those through
the API.
events_MessageSecurityCompletedEvent.title: MessageSecurityCompletedEvent

events_MessageSecurityReviewEvent.description:
In hold mode, Agent Armor held a received message for review: your agents are not sent its `message.received`
until someone releases it. The message carries the `agent-armor-held` label until then. Sent once per message and
inbox; `event_id` is stable. Not sent for messages labeled `spam`, `blocked`, `unauthenticated`, or `trash`: list
held mail by the `agent-armor-held` label instead.
events_MessageSecurityReviewEvent.title: MessageSecurityReviewEvent

events_MessageSecurityOverride.description: The message someone released, and the record of the release. Fetch the message for its content.
events_MessageSecurityOverride.title: MessageSecurityOverride

events_MessageSecurityOverrideEvent.description:
Someone released a message Agent Armor held for review. Its `message.received` is sent to your agents as well,
and the two can arrive in either order.
Sent once per message and inbox; `event_id` is stable. Not sent for messages labeled `spam`, `blocked`,
`unauthenticated`, or `trash`.
events_MessageSecurityOverrideEvent.title: MessageSecurityOverrideEvent

events_MessageOpenedEvent.description:
A tracked message was opened for the first time. Sent once per message: repeat opens do not
resend it.
events_MessageOpenedEvent.title: MessageOpenedEvent

event_id.description: Equals the `operation_id` returned by the request that made the change.

events_CalendarEventCreatedEvent.description:
An event was created, through the API or from an invitation the inbox received. Also sent when
one date of a recurring event is edited for the first time; `calendar_event` is then that date.
events_CalendarEventCreatedEvent.title: CalendarEventCreatedEvent

events_CalendarEventPrevious.description:
The values that a `calendar.event.updated` change replaced, for the fields it changed. Only
changed fields appear; a field that had no value before the change is absent.
events_CalendarEventPrevious.title: CalendarEventPrevious

event_id.description: Equals the `operation_id` returned by the request that made the change.

previous.description: For changes to a one-off or series event, the prior values of the fields that changed.

events_CalendarEventUpdatedEvent.description:
An event, or one or more dates of a recurring event, changed. `calendar_event` is the event
(or the date) after the change. Cancelling dates with a delete on a dated ID also sends this
event, with the cancelled date as `calendar_event`.
events_CalendarEventUpdatedEvent.title: CalendarEventUpdatedEvent

event_id.description: Equals the `deletion_id` returned by the request that made the change.

events_CalendarEventDeletedEvent.description:
A one-off or recurring event was deleted. `calendar_event` is the event as it was. Cancelling
dates of a recurring event sends `calendar.event.updated` instead.
events_CalendarEventDeletedEvent.title: CalendarEventDeletedEvent

events_CalendarEventRespondedEvent.description:
An attendee's response changed: the inbox responded with the respond endpoint, or an attendee
replied by email to an invitation the inbox sent. `calendar_event.attendees` holds the new
statuses.
events_CalendarEventRespondedEvent.title: CalendarEventRespondedEvent

event_id.description: Stable for this date and boundary. Use it to deduplicate deliveries.

calendar_event.description: The event or date as it stood when the boundary was first processed.

scheduled_at.description: The start this webhook is for (the event's `start_at`).

events_CalendarEventStartingEvent.description:
An event, or one date of a recurring event, has started. Usually sent within a minute after
`scheduled_at`. If a date is first picked up after it has already ended and more than 5
minutes after its start (for example, an event created entirely in the past), neither its
`calendar.event.starting` nor its `calendar.event.ending` is sent. Retries carry the same
`event_id` and an identical body.
events_CalendarEventStartingEvent.title: CalendarEventStartingEvent

event_id.description: Stable for this date and boundary. Use it to deduplicate deliveries.

calendar_event.description: The event or date as it stood when the boundary was first processed.

scheduled_at.description: The end this webhook is for (the event's `end_at`).

events_CalendarEventEndingEvent.description:
An event, or one date of a recurring event, has ended. Usually sent within a minute after
`scheduled_at`. Retries carry the same `event_id` and an identical body.
events_CalendarEventEndingEvent.title: CalendarEventEndingEvent
